findings.current: “He lasted four hours while being beaten like that. With stamina and grit like his, he’ll recover in no time… Why are you laughing?”
findings.defect: The draft invents recovery as the result of Taekyung’s stamina and grit, while the source leaves Mukyung’s thought unfinished and therefore ambiguous.
findings.rationale: The Korean breaks off after 금방 without specifying whether Taekyung will recover, improve, or accomplish something else.
findings.replacement: “He lasted four hours while taking a beating like that. With that kind of stamina and grit, he’ll soon… Why are you laughing?”
findings.source: “그렇게 두들겨 맞으면서도 두 시진이나 버티더군요. 이 정도 체력과 독기면 금방…… 왜 웃으십니까?”

findings.current: Jin Mukyung silently looked down at him sprawled out on the floor, then slowly opened his mouth.
findings.defect: The draft omits that Taekyung is lying spread-eagled in the shape of the character 大.
findings.rationale: 대자로 뻗은 explicitly describes the position of Taekyung’s body, and the visual detail contributes to the aftermath of the blow.
findings.replacement: Jin Mukyung silently looked down at him lying spread-eagled on the floor, then slowly spoke.
findings.source: 대자로 뻗은 그를 말없이 내려다보던 진무경이 천천히 입을 열었다.

findings.current: I casually turned my head and saw Jin Mukyung staring at me with round eyes.
findings.defect: “Round eyes” suggests surprise or innocence, whereas 고리눈을 뜬 describes a fierce, glaring expression.
findings.rationale: The source presents Mukyung as visibly hostile, which motivates Taekyung’s immediate recollection of the previous beating.
findings.replacement: I casually turned my head and found Jin Mukyung glaring at me.
findings.source: 슬쩍 고개를 돌리니 고리눈을 뜬 진무경이 보였다.

findings.current: “Oh? Hyung. When did you get here?”
findings.defect: The draft uses the casual “Hyung” even though 형님 and the surrounding polite speech mark Taekyung’s deliberate shift to deference.
findings.rationale: The next paragraph explicitly identifies Taekyung’s use of 존댓말 as a calculated attempt to avoid another beating, and the established rendering for his deferential 형님 is “Hyung-nim.”
findings.replacement: “Oh? Hyung-nim. When did you get here?”

findings.defect: The casual address again removes the formal deference Taekyung is intentionally maintaining.
findings.rationale: 형님 is deferential here, and Taekyung’s exaggerated politeness is the scene’s central comic strategy.

findings.current: *Logout is impossible during combat? What kind of bullshit is that?*
findings.defect: “Bullshit” adds explicit profanity absent from this thought and unnecessarily intensifies Taekyung’s register.
findings.rationale: 그딴 게 어디 있어 is dismissive and indignant, but it is not itself a profanity.
findings.replacement: *You can’t Logout during combat? What kind of ridiculous rule is that?*
findings.source: ‘전투 시에는 로그아웃이 불가능하다니. 그딴 게 어디 있어.’

findings.current:
“Why are your eyes like that?”

“My eyes?”

At his icy voice, I opened my eyes as brightly as possible.

Now even my eyes had to look well-behaved if I wanted to take one less beating.
findings.defect: The exchange is rendered in unnatural English: Mukyung is objecting to how Taekyung is looking at him, and “eyes had to look well-behaved” does not naturally convey Taekyung’s attempt to look bright and innocent.
findings.rationale: 눈을 그렇게 뜨다 concerns Taekyung’s expression or gaze, while 초롱초롱 and 착하게 describe his calculated attempt to make that gaze appear harmless.
findings.replacement:
“Why are you looking at me like that?”

“Me?”

At his icy tone, I made my eyes look as bright and innocent as possible.

Now I even had to watch how I looked at him if I wanted one less beating.
findings.source:
“너 왜 눈을 그렇게 떠?”

“제가요?”

싸늘한 목소리에 최대한 눈을 초롱초롱하게 떴다. 이제는 눈도 착하게 떠야 한 대라도 덜 맞는다.

findings.current: Wasn’t this a younger brother without even a speck of virtue?
findings.defect: “Virtue” narrowly implies moral righteousness and sounds stilted; 장점 means any merit, good point, or redeeming quality.
findings.rationale: Mukyung is denying that Taekyung has anything praiseworthy, not making a formal judgment about his virtue.
findings.replacement: Wasn’t he a younger brother without a single redeeming quality?

findings.defect: The past-tense phrasing is unnatural and weakens Mukyung’s dismissive reassurance about the present possibility of death.
findings.rationale: The Korean rhetorically dismisses the possibility that Taekyung will die from the beating.
findings.replacement: “It’s not like he’s going to die.”

findings.current: Jin Wikyung had no doubt that the two geniuses would become a powerful stimulus for each other.
findings.defect: “Become a powerful stimulus for each other” is an unnatural Korean-syntax calque.
findings.rationale: 큰 자극이 되다 naturally means that each will motivate or push the other, which “spur each other on” conveys without changing the relationship.
findings.replacement: Jin Wikyung had no doubt that the two geniuses would greatly spur each other on.
findings.source: 두 천재가 서로에게 큰 자극이 될 것임을, 그는 믿어 의심치 않았다.

summary: The draft alters one facial expression, resolves an intentionally unfinished statement, drops a visual action detail, weakens deferential address, adds profanity, and contains several localized wording issues.
